MATTHEW.|21}}</noinclude>that the boate vvas couered vvith vvaues, but he slept. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=25}}† And they came to him, and raised him, saying, Lord, saue vs, vve perish. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=26}}† And he saith to them, Why are you fearful O ye of litle faith? Then rising vp {{sup|‖}} he commaunded the vvindes & the sea, and there ensued a great calme. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=27}}† Moreouer the men marueled saying, What an one is this, for the vvindes and the sea obey him?⊣

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=28}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 5, 1. Luc. 8, 26.''}}* vvhen he was come beyond the vvater into the countrey of the Gerasens, there mette him tvvo that had diuels, coming forth out of the sepulcres, exceding fierce, so that none could passe by that vvay. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=29}}† And behold they cried saying, What is betvvene vs and thee {{sc|Iesv}} the sonne of God? art thou come hither to torment vs before the time? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=30}}† And there vvas not farre frome them an heard of many swine feeding. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=31}}† And the diuels besought him saying, If thou cast vs out, send vs into the heard of swine. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=32}}† And he said to thē, Goe. But they going forth vvent into the svvine, and behold the whole heard vvent vvith a violence headlong into the sea: and they dyed in the waters. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=33}}† And the svvineheardes fled: and comming into the citie, told al, and of them that had been possessed of diuels. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=34}}† And behold the vvhole citie vvent out to meete {{sc|Iesvs}}, and vvhen they savv him, they besought him that he vvould passe from their quarters.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. VIII.}}}}

''4. Priest.''] The Priests of the old law (saith S. Chrysostome) had authoritie and priuilege only to discerne who where healed of leprosie, and to denounce the same to the people: but the Priests of the new law haue power to purge in very deede the filth of the soule. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Priests forgiue sinnes.}}Therfore whosoeuer despiseth them, is more vvorthie to be punished then the rebel Dathan and his complices. ''S. Chryso. li. 3. de Sacerd''.

''4. Gift.''] Our Sauiour willeth him to goe and offer his gift or sacrifice according as Moyses prescribed in that case, because the other sacrifice being the holiest of al holies, which is his body, was not yet begonne. So saith ''S. Aug. li. 2. q. Euang. q. 3. & Cont. Aduers. leg. & Proph. li. 1. c. 19. 20''.

''8. Not worthy.''] ''Orig. ho. 5. in diuers''. When thou eatest (saith he) and drinkest the body and bloud of our Lord, he entereth vnder thy roofe. Thou also therfore humbling thy self, say: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|Domine}}, non sum dignus.}}Lord I am not worthy. &c. So said {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=* ''Liturg. S. Chrys. Græc. sub finem''.}}S. Chrysostom in his Masse. and so doeth the Cath. Churche vse at this day in euery Masse. See S. Augustine ''ep. 118 ad Ianu''.

''14. His wiues mother.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Priests mariage.}}Of Peter specially among the rest it is euident that he had a wife, but (as S. Hierom sayth) after they were called to be Apostles, they had no more carnal companie with their wiues, as he proueth there by the very wordes of our Sauiour, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lib. 1. adu. Iou. c. 14. Mt. 19, 29. Epiph. hæ. 59.''}}* ''He that hath left wife &c''. And so in the Latin Churche hath been alwayes vsed, that maried men may be and are daily made Priests, either after the death of the wife, or with her consent to liue in perpetual continencie. And if the Greekes haue Priests that doe otherwise, S. Epiphanius a Greeke Doctor telleth them that they doe it agaynst the ancient Canons, and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=* ''Sozom. li. 1. c. 22. Socrat. li. 1 c. 8''.}}* Paphnutius plainely signifieth the same in the first Councel of Nice. But this is most playne, that there was neuer either in the Greeke Church or the Latin, authentical example of any that married after holy Orders.

''22. Let the dead.''] By this we see that not only no wordly or carnal respect, but no other laudable<noinclude>{{rh||C iij|dutie}}</noinclude>
